summary: This room is a tight, mostly-healthy DSP-theory neighborhood built around the 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer and its satellites (Dissolutions, Three Kinds of Warp, Rank-N Lattice Analysis, Volterra Kernels, Dispersion Table, LPC, Phase Reduction) plus the browser-instrument track (Wavetable Scanner, Waveguide Synthesizer, Tract Mirror, Three.js). It is already well-cross-linked internally — the Dissolutions hub in particular is doing exactly the de-sprawl job a hub should do, gathering seven "same object, two doorways" insights instead of letting each sit isolated. Given Loudon's "cluttered" note this morning, I looked hard for merge/compost candidates and didn't find genuine ones: the apparent duplication (concept entry vs. artifact entry, e.g. 1D Wavetable Scanning vs. Wavetable Scanner, or LPC vs. Tract Mirror) is a deliberate and stated split, not sprawl. The one real piece of clutter I found is small and literal: Tract Mirror declares two separate link types to the same target (Linear Predictive Coding). The more interesting work this pass turned up is outward-facing: Tract Mirror sits inside this room with zero inbound despite being the most concrete proof-of-thesis in the cluster, and two newcomers outside the room — control-vocabulary-math and Quadratic Interpolation in DSP — turn out to be worked answers to open questions this room's entries pose out loud (the "hardest problem" of high-dimensional control-surface design, and the linear-vs-quadratic-vs-cubic wavetable interpolation question) but haven't yet found.

typed_relations.rationale: Synthesis Topologies §3 already names the torus project's seven-surface design as its concrete exemplar of the 'fixed-skeleton-variable-flesh' in-between category, but the torus entry's own frontmatter has no pointer back to the general framework it instantiates. Direction invariant: exemplifies points to the ground (the general entry).
typed_relations.evidence: "Fixed-skeleton-variable-flesh designs (2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's seven surfaces)." — Synthesis Topologies §3

typed_relations.rationale: Chebyshev is Fourier's own Forward Vectors names the 'wavelet → modal → rank-N-lattice family' it wants to join, but the frontmatter link runs only one direction (Rank-N Lattice Analysis → Chebyshev is Fourier, label choose-your-basis).
typed_relations.evidence: "Map the full Fourier → wavelet → modal → rank-N-lattice family as a single 'choose-your-basis' entry; this dissolution is one member of it."

typed_relations.rationale: Dispersion Table's whole generalization (store phase-response curves, not waveforms) is built directly on Waveguide Synthesizer's physics scaffolding, but Waveguide Synthesizer doesn't point forward to what it made possible.
typed_relations.evidence: "See [[Waveguide Synthesizer]] for the physics scaffolding (D'Alembert's traveling-wave solution, the delay-line architecture, Karplus-Strong as the lossy case)." — Dispersion Table

typed_relations.rationale: LPC declares this mirrors link explicitly ('LPC's lattice and the digital waveguide are the same structure read from opposite ends'), and Tract Mirror carries the same claim from a third angle, but Waveguide Synthesizer's own frontmatter is silent on it — the triangle is missing its third leg.
typed_relations.evidence: "That is why the link to [[Waveguide Synthesizer]] is a mirrors and not a passing reference: the vocal tract and the plucked string are one piece of mathematics wearing two bodies." — Linear Predictive Coding

typed_relations.rationale: Tract Mirror carries 0 inbound despite being the room's most concrete proof-of-thesis. Tract Mirror already declares mirrors → Waveguide Synthesizer ('the-tube-to-its-string'); the reciprocal is the cheapest, most honest inbound wire available.
typed_relations.evidence: "Where the [[Waveguide Synthesizer]] renders the string body of this mathematics in the browser, Tract Mirror renders the tube body." — Tract Mirror

typed_relations.rationale: Tract Mirror is literally LPC's central thesis built into a shipped VST — the strongest spawned relation in the room, and it answers LPC's own open question about whether the source-filter identity is only a prose claim. Currently only Tract Mirror points back (emerged-from); LPC has no forward pointer to what it produced.
typed_relations.evidence: "The thesis is the mirrors link from [[Linear Predictive Coding]] to [[Waveguide Synthesizer]], executed: the LPC lattice filter's reflection coefficients are the impedance mismatches between successive tube segments." — Tract Mirror

typed_relations.rationale: Tract Mirror's GUI is a WKWebView running three.js — Three.js's first job that leaves the browser proper. Tract Mirror declares couples-with → Three.js; worth the reciprocal so Three.js's own roster names its native-plugin job.
typed_relations.evidence: "JUCE 8 + WebView GUI — C++ DSP core; the GUI is a WKWebView running three.js, so every interim mockup artifact is a step toward the real interface." — Tract Mirror

typed_relations.rationale: Both entries land on the same design question — what interpolation order a wavetable read needs — from opposite directions. Quadratic Interpolation in DSP frames quadratic as the theoretical sweet spot and asks (open question 1) whether cubic is worth it; 1D Wavetable Scanning ran the experiment on a shipped Sketch and found plain linear sufficient, reserving anything higher-order for briefs that name audible aliasing as the problem. Genuine live tension, not a forced link.
typed_relations.evidence: "Higher-order interpolation has aliasing-control upsides for very small frame counts, but at typical 8-256-frame tables the linear blend's audible artifact ceiling is below the table's authoring noise. Reach for cubic only when a brief names 'audibly aliasing morph' as the problem." — 1D Wavetable Scanning, Lost Branches

typed_relations.rationale: This entry names 'control-surface design for high-dimensional spaces' as the suite's single hardest, most valuable, unsolved problem. control-vocabulary-math is a shipped, worked instance of exactly that problem solved for a sibling instrument — a noisy N-neuron Kuramoto population reduced to four performable knobs (K, sigma_threshold, mean firing rate, and the order parameter r as both readout and control term).
typed_relations.evidence: "A 256-dimensional latent space, a family of triply-periodic minimal surfaces, a persistence diagram — each is a rich object with no existing performance vocabulary... That invention — not the DSP — is where the value and the difficulty concentrate." — Infeasible DSP Now Shippable; "This document formalizes the layer that sits on top of that engine: the statistical descriptors that turn a noisy crowd of N spiking neurons into four or five smooth, performable knobs." — control-vocabulary-math

typed_relations.rationale: Phase Reduction's forward vector asks to make the Phase Response Curve 'a designed control object' atop Kuramoto coupling. control-vocabulary-math independently built exactly that move for a different instrument — the order parameter r is simultaneously the meter and a term inside the dynamics, the same self-referential design Phase Reduction is reaching for.
typed_relations.evidence: "Use the PRC explicitly as a designed control object in the coupled-grain / granular-additive hybrid." — Phase Reduction, Forward Vectors; "the single quantity that closes the loop between all of them is r... simultaneously a read-out and a term inside the dynamics, so the instrument's coherence is literally self-referential." — control-vocabulary-math

coherence_findings.issue: Tract Mirror declares two separate typed links to the same target (Linear Predictive Coding): emerged-from/'mirror-made-playable' and mirrors/'the-lattice-made-playable'. Two different relation types to one target, doing overlapping work — a small, literal instance of the clutter Loudon flagged this morning.
coherence_findings.proposed_action: Keep emerged-from (the true lineage fact — Tract Mirror grew out of the LPC entry). Drop the mirrors duplicate; the mirrors relationship to LPC is already fully carried structurally by Waveguide Synthesizer↔LPC (proposed above) and by Tract Mirror's own mirrors link to Waveguide Synthesizer ('the-tube-to-its-string').

entry_health_flags.vector_issue: none — forward_vector is specific and load-bearing
entry_health_flags.graffiti_note: 15 inbound links and cited as the shared spine by Volterra Kernels, Rank-N Lattice Analysis, Dispersion Table, Torus Warping Catalog, and Chebyshev is Fourier. It is functioning as the room's foundational reference, not a first-draft sprout.
Structural problem, not a content one: 0 inbound despite being the clearest built proof of the LPC/Waveguide mirrors thesis in the whole room. See typed_relations for the proposed wiring.

open_question_resolutions.question: How is the morphing implemented across surfaces — crossfading c_mn coefficients in spectral space, or crossfading W directly in spatial space?
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: 2D Wavetable Catalog's own open question already names spectral-domain interpolation as the right tool for cross-symmetry surface morphs (Membrane↔Chladni) — pull that decision up as the working answer instead of carrying it as two separate open questions.

open_question_resolutions.question: Cubic vs. quadratic in oscillators: is the extra cost justified for audio, or is quadratic sufficient?
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: 1D Wavetable Scanning already ran this experiment on a shipped Sketch and found linear sufficient, cubic reserved for briefs naming audible aliasing. Cross-link (see typed_relations) so the open question cites a real shipped data point instead of staying purely theoretical.

open_question_resolutions.question: Invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces (the recurring 'hardest problem')
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Link Rank-N Lattice Analysis and Infeasible DSP Now Shippable to control-vocabulary-math as a worked example rather than treating the control-vocabulary problem as wholly unsolved territory.

open_question_resolutions.question: Document the meta-pattern: Loudon's intuitions about framework-kinship keep getting confirmed — worth its own note if a third instance lands.
open_question_resolutions.verdict: unconfirmed third instance — do not force
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Volterra Kernels and the Torus is mirrors-linked from Phase Reduction as 'unification-via-identity,' but its own body doesn't narrate an intuition-first genesis the way Chebyshev is Fourier and Phase Reduction do explicitly. Before spinning up a meta-entry, check the source session for whether the hunch actually came first — don't count it as instance three on the strength of the pattern alone.

open_question_resolutions.question: Seed the wider theme entry 'The Right Representation Reveals the Symmetry' that this and the log-scaling/Ohm's-Law material can both link into (currently a ghost).
open_question_resolutions.proposed_action: Dissolutions already names, as ingredient 2 of every dissolution, 'a reframing — typically a coordinate change, a basis change, a timescale rescaling, or a representational shift — that surfaces a single underlying object.' That is the same claim the ghost hub would make. Rather than planting a second hub, fold 'the right representation reveals the symmetry' into Dissolutions' own prose as the name for ingredient 2 — one hub doing the job instead of two doing half each.
